Players take turns choosing a role (Settler, Builder, Mayor, Craftsman, Trader, Captain or Prospector) and performing the associated action. While each of the other players also has the chance to perform the role’s functions, only the player who chooses the role will be awarded the special privilege associated with it. Victory points earned for buildings. Victory point tokens earned at the captain phase. Conditional victory points earned at the end of the game for occupied large buildings. Rules summary The game is played over several rounds. At the start of a round, the governor selects a role, then each player in turn selects a role. At the end of the round, the governor token moves to the next player. When a role has been chosen, each player in turn plays the action for this role. Only the player who selected the role can use the role privilege. Roles Note: occupied violet buildings have modifier effects for role actions. Mayor Colonists set foot in the new world! Privilege : the mayor can get one more colonist from the supply. Action : in turn, beginning with the mayor, players get one colonist from the ship, until it is empty. Then players have to set colonists on their buildings and plantations. Craftsman Goods are produced. Privilege : the craftsman can produce one more good of their choice. Action : produce goods for your occupied buildings and plantations. Trader Goods are sold to the trading house. Privilege : the trader earns 1 extra doubloon if they sell. Action : sell one good the trading house doesn't have yet. Settler Plantations settlement. Privilege : the settler can get a quarry instead of a plantation. Action : get a plantation chosen among those available. Builder Buildings are bought and built. Privilege : the builder can get a building for 1 doubloon less than the regular price. Action : get a building chosen among those available. Captain Victory points are won by shipping goods to the old world. Privilege : the captain earns one extra victory points if they ship some goods. Action : select a type of good to load on a cargo ship; 1 victory point is earned for each barrel of this type of good loaded on the ship. Prospector Gold rush brings money! Privilege : the prospector gets one doubloon from the bank. Action : none. Game End Game end is triggered at the end of the round by any of: Not enough colonists in the supply to refill the colonist ship at the end of the mayor phase. The number of colonists refilled equals to the total number of unoccupied circles on each player's buildings, at the end of each round. The last victory point token has been earned during the captain phase. At least one of the players built on their 12th and last free space in the city. Scoring In case of a tie, the player owning the most doubloons and goods is the winner. Choosing a role Tool tips are available to give information on roles and buildings by hovering over game elements. Select the role of your choice in the list on the right of your game board. Mayor : accept or refuse to get an extra colonist from the supply. Colonists are then automatically recruited by players. Click on a building or a plantation to setup a colonist on it. [Rating: 1/10] Don´t believe twe hype! I have played it a couple of time but can´t see what the fuss is, it plays the same almost every time, it is easy to get screwed early in the game, there is virtually no interaction between players (except shouting; take that tile or he will get it thus...), and the mechanisms has been seen in both Princes of Florence and Ohne Furst und Adel (Citadels) before. Boring, boring...

[Rating: 1/10] Kinda boring....   Not much action.... What is the big deal with this game? Is it the cool little wood pieces!?  I think everyone in our group, even the owner, went through a little anti-climax once we had played it.  Sorry, simply over-rated.

[Rating: 1/10] despite anything john brier might say this game is terrible.  Yes, my opinion could have something to do with the utter domination that he has over the game.

[Rating: 1/10] Only played this once thus far.  Actually hated the game until close to the end.  Part of that may have been the quality of instruction (or lack thereof) by the game's owner.  Has lots of neat features & mechanics, so I'd definitely give it another try.  Not at the top of my must-play list though.

[Rating: 1/10] Not   my   number 1 game but then I need to play it a few more times to get more out of it I think.  Learnt a lot from playing virtual opponents but my group seem to prefer San Juan. It dawned on me that I was playing as a slave owner sometime after playing this, so I sold it. The new editions seem to also be problematic so I am steering clear.

[Rating: 1/10] Dry. Dull. Not exciting at all. If the first move is *always* the same one, where's the fun? Pales in comparison to other role selection games, especially Race for the Galaxy.

[Rating: 1/10] Oh gosh, I played it and it's really bad. No fun at all and winning is essentially at the sake of the other players.  [i]Old comment: I will never play a game which incorporates slavery in such a naive way.

[Rating: 1/10] Played it just once. Couldn't get my opponents to finish the game; it was a struggle from beginning to end trying to keep them interested. Needless to say, I will never play it again. Game is waaaaaay over-rated.

[Rating: 1/10] Ever have a game you hate for no logical reason? Well Puerto Rico is that game for me. I really hate the game! The kind of hate usually reserved only for the lowest levels of hell. Unfortunately, everyone else I know likes this game, and so we play it on a regular basis.

[Rating: 1/10] This appears to be one of those games you either love or hate.  I'm sorry, I'm probably swimming upstream, but in the 4-5 times I've played it, I have formed an extremely negative opinion of the game.  The Turn order always messes me up.  The guy in front of me invariably takes what will screw me over or what I need the most.  I just don't get the strategy or the appeal of the game.  You could not pay me to play it. [Rating: 1/10] Horrible learning curve. Incredibly anti-intuitive and badly flowing. UPDATE: played more & won. The most wrongly played game in the world. Suffers from "who is playing on my right" syndrome.  Stupid 'less choices per turn" mechanic. Lot's of fiddly bits help make it too long for set-up/teardown. Smoke and mirrors. 15 PAGES of geek rules questions. And these are just the OBJECTIVE criticisms. Just ask for more. It ain't number 1- Haven't seen it played anywhere in several years.
